The working file is the complete analysis; the reports are its reader copies. Each should be read in full — this message is not the analysis.

**Bottom line:** At today's valuations (Shiller CAPE ~41 vs. a 17.8 historical average), the "stocks beat a 6.25% mortgage" framing is backwards — paying down principal is mathematically a guaranteed, tax-free 6.25% APR (~6.43% effective) return, while the best available forward-looking model (Vanguard, 4.2%–6.2% nominal) implies only a ~3.4%–5.1% after-tax return on the index fund, a negative expected risk premium for staying invested instead of paying down debt. The recommendation is a split tilted toward paydown — illustratively ~70% ($42,000) to principal, ~30% ($18,000) invested — rather than 100% of either, because the expected-value edge for paydown, while real, isn't large enough to justify giving up all liquidity. Confidence is MEDIUM: the conclusion would flip if realized equity returns over the next decade exceed roughly 7.6%/year, which is above Vanguard's entire current forecast range.
